- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast windows.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is positive or neutral, particularly after recent spikes.  
- Overshoot after sharp upward sentiment spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.  
- Mean-revert forecasts when sentiment shows prolonged negative drift; adjust downward by 1–3% per 3–5 day negative sentiment window.  
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delay) are overestimated in short-term forecasts; apply a 1–2% downward correction for 1–3 day ahead forecasts.  
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast variance by 10–15% in high-sentiment volatility windows.
